hook: A 125,000-year-old Arabian lakeshore site holds stone points with poison residue from hunting.

readout.label: Approximate age of the Arabian site

summary: At 'Uruq Aljelibah in Saudi Arabia, stone tools show use-wear, impact damage and residues of a poisonous plant, Acokanthera schimperi, alongside bones of hippo, buffalo, camel and other large animals. This suggests hafted, poisoned weapons and plant processing by early humans on a green Arabia. The tool makers are not identified from fossils, and one site cannot show how widespread the practice was.
title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore.
